title: John had an external write-command; Teach all nations includes the pen
source_text: XII. Neque tamen Joanni saltem defuit externum mandatum; ipse enim in Apocalypsi testatur pluribus in locis sibi coelitus injunctum, ut scriberet ea quae Dominus ipsi revelaverat, ac praesertim Epistolas illas quas, Christi nomine, septem Ecclesiis Asiae inscribit. Non recte autem opponit Bellarminus mandatum docendi, quod Apostoli a Christo habuerunt, mandato scribendi: Docet enim non tantum qui viva voce instituit, sed etiam qui doctrinam scripto tradit: Ideoque quod discipulis suis injungit Christus Mat. cap. ult. Docete omnes Gentes, ad solam praedicationem viva voce factam restringi non debet, sed ad scriptionem ipsam potest extendi, quae unus est ex docendi modis. Nam ibi jubet Christus ut optimis quibusque modis gentes Evangelii cognitione imbuerent, sive sermone & lingua, sive etiam calamo.
pass_a_gloss: Nor yet did John at least lack an external mandate; for he himself in the Apocalypse testifies in several places that it was enjoined on him from heaven to write the things the Lord had revealed to him, and especially those Letters which, in Christ's name, he addresses to the seven churches of Asia. But Bellarmine does not rightly oppose the mandate of teaching, which the Apostles had from Christ, to the mandate of writing: For he teaches not only who instructs by living voice, but also who hands on doctrine in writing: And therefore what Christ enjoins on his disciples in the last chapter of Matthew — Teach all nations — ought not to be restricted to preaching done by living voice alone, but can be extended to writing itself, which is one of the modes of teaching. For there Christ orders that by the best means whatever they should imbue the nations with knowledge of the Gospel, whether by speech and tongue, or also by the pen.
pass_b_english: John's Apocalypse repeatedly records a heavenly order to write — including the seven Asian letters.
Bellarmine's split between 'teach' and 'write' fails: teaching includes the pen.
Matthew's closing 'Teach all nations' is not viva-voce-only; writing is one teaching mode.
Christ wants the nations filled with the Gospel by speech or by calamus.

rejected: oral teaching alone fulfills the charge
